articles.title: Australia keep faith in Marnus Labuschagne as Test squad for South Africa tour named
articles.summary: Under-pressure batter retains place for three-Test series. Squad provides ‘balance and options’, says George Bailey. Australian selectors have stuck with struggling batter Marnus Labuschagne for next month’s Test tour of South Africa.
body: Fast bowler Michael Neser, spinner Matthew Kuhnemann and batter Cooper Connolly will join the group for the series starting in Durban on 9 October.

Labuschagne was ICC’s top-ranked Test batter in 2023, but has struggled for runs in the years since with his last century coming in the 2023 Ashes. He averaged 25 in last summer’s Ashes, and then had scores of 1, 31 and 4 in the recent Tests against Bangladesh.
The 32-year-old will be competing with Josh Inglis and Connolly, the 23-year-old who has been tipped for a bright future.

Connolly has played one Test for Australia last year in Sri Lanka, as well as matches in T20 and ODI formats. He will be in South Africa for the ODI series prior to the Tests in a squad named last week notable for its omission of Labuschagne.
points: Squad provides ‘balance and options’, says George Bailey.
Australian selectors have stuck with struggling batter Marnus Labuschagne for next month’s Test tour of South Africa.
Fast bowler Michael Neser, spinner Matthew Kuhnemann and batter Cooper Connolly will join the group for the series starting in Durban on 9 October.

articles.title: US overcome poor shooting and Italy’s eye-poke claims in edgy Fiba World Cup win
articles.summary: USA edge into quarter’s with nervy 55-52 win. Cecilia Zandalasini claims she was poked in eye. Caitlin Clark shoots 0-6 from the field. Jackie Young had a big fourth quarter and Breanna Stewart made her only basket of the game to put ⁠the United States up for good, helping the Americans escape with…
body: The ​US (2-0), who clinched a quarter-final berth with the victory, led only 42-39 after three quarters and fell behind by two points on three occasions in the fourth. Stewart’s jumper, assisted by Young, gave the Americans a 51-50 lead with 3:20 to go, and Young hit a ⁠floater on their next possession. Chelsea Gray made a pull-up with 1:07 left for an ​important cushion, but Italy hit a quick ‌two-pointer in response to ‌cut it to 55-52. Gray missed a shot on the next US trip but Young ‌corralled the rebound to help her team bleed more clock.

Italy’s Cecilia Zandalasini, who missed a three-pointer to tie the game with three seconds left, was seen shouting at the referees after the buzzer as she argued she had been poked in the eye on the play. She expressed contrition after the game.

“I would like to apologize for how I reacted in the end,” said Zandalasini. “To the opposing team, it was a lot of emotions today, but I should have kept them inside of me a little better. I want to apologize to the referees. It’s just when I wear this jersey, it’s just a different beast that comes out of me, and now I feel embarrassed for how I reacted.”

articles.title: European football: Lamine Yamal’s double powers Barcelona to rout of Valencia
articles.summary: Gatti’s stoppage-time header rescues Juve against Milan. Goalkeeper Koeman Jr scores two penalties in Eredivisie. Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.
body: The reigning champions moved three points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday. Fermín López, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick’s swaggering visitors on a hot afternoon on Spain’s east coast.
Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia’s fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium.

“We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team,” said Flick. “We stay calm and then if it’s possible to score we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us. Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it’s perfect then you can stop working.”

articles.title: Richard Hughes confirmed as Al-Hilal sporting director after Liverpool departure
articles.summary: Hughes joins Saudi exodus after two years at Anfield. Martinelli, Summerville and Watkins are at Al-Hilal. Richard Hughes has been appointed as the sporting director ⁠of Al-Hilal, the Saudi Pro League club confirmed on ⁠Sunday, following ⁠his ​ departure from Liverpool.
body: Hughes, 47, joined Liverpool in 2024 from Bournemouth. ⁠He appointed Arne Slot as Jürgen Klopp’s successor as head coach, ⁠a decision that paid immediate dividends ​as the Reds ‌claimed the ‌Premier League title in 2024-25. Slot ‌was sacked and replaced by Andoni Iraola in June.

“The appointment of Hughes came as part of Al-Hilal’s efforts to strengthen its football system ‌and develop its sporting structure with specialised expertise,” the Saudi Pro League leaders ​said in a statement.

The appointment highlights Al-Hilal’s drive to tap into English football, with Hughes the latest ⁠former Premier League figure to join ​the ​Riyadh-based club. Hughes follows players Gabriel ​Martinelli, Crysencio Summerville and ​ Ollie Watkins, ‌who joined ​the ​Saudi club this summer from Arsenal, West Ham United and Aston Villa, respectively. Al-Hilal’s manager is Simone Inzaghi, formerly of Inter.

Two members of Liverpool’s recruitment department are set to follow Hughes to Al Hilal. Mark Burchill and Craig McKee, who joined Liverpool from Bournemouth with Hughes two years ago, are now poised to team up with the Scot in Saudi.

articles.title: Mets Reliever Has Been Elite Since Making His Debut
articles.summary: 26-year-old reliever Nate Lavender made his MLB debut for the New York Mets on August 4th. In his first appearance as a Met, Lavender threw 1 1/3 scoreless innings. He only gave up one walk and recorded his first career strikeout the same night.
body: In May of his 2024 season, Lavender had to get Tommy John surgery and ultimately miss the rest of the 2024 season. Lavender was later selected by the Tampa Bay Rays in the Rule 5 draft, ending his first tenure in the Mets organization. While with the Rays, Lavender didn’t do any pitching with them, as he was still recovering from surgery during the 2025 season. He was then DFA’d on November 6, 2025. Lavender returned to the Mets just a few days later. He had a solid stint in Triple-A earlier this season, and the rest is history.

If Lavender continues to do what he has been doing for the last 20-plus games of this season, there should be no question that he will have a spot on this roster in 2027. Even if it has been a smaller sample size with only 12 games, he has made his presence known and has shown he can come into different situations and get the out when needed. The Mets would be out of their minds not to have a spot for Lavender on the roster for 2027. A solid lefty out of the bullpen is a big need for any MLB team, and Lavender has shown he can compete time and time again.

articles.title: Shavkat Rakhmonov reflects on fighting Ian Machado Garry with injured knee: ‘That’s the Kazakh way’
articles.summary: It’s been nearly two years since Shavkat Rakhmonov has fought and the guy is still dealing with endless knee injuries. The Kazakh fighter was a top UFC welterweight contender and even managed to get a title fight booked against then-champ Belal Muhammad.
body: Now, 21 months later, Rakhmonov is still wearing a massive knee brace in a new interview with ALF Global where he discussed his choice to fight injured.

“We are bound to make plenty of mistakes,” he said. “If you really look at it, I also made a wide variety of mistakes throughout my sports career. I actually shouldn’t have even fought Ian Machado Garry at all. With injuries like that, I shouldn’t have fought at all. I just took a risk.”
“That’s the Kazakh way. Kazakhs are very daring. They’re not afraid. If it had been some other Dagestani fighter like Khabib or Islam Makhachev, they definitely would’ve refused.”

“I already had an injury going into the Ian Garry fight,” he added. “I stepped up, I hadn’t fought for a year, I wanted to fight. Even before that, I had health problems, too, and it turned out there were only two weeks left before the Ian Garry fight. That old injury was still bothering me a lot. My leg was swollen.”

articles.title: No new striker, no worries - Havertz and Odegaard torment Chelsea
articles.summary: Nine points from three games, one goal conceded and big players stepping up - are Arsenal still ahead of the rest in the race for the Premier League title?
body: Arsenal shelled out close to £200m on new signings during the summer transfer window but fell short of landing the elite forward they craved.

Former Manchester City goalscorer Julian Alvarez was on their radar but remains at Atletico Madrid, while the Gunners were also interested in Aston Villa 's Morgan Rogers, Paris St-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Vinicius Jr.
While Rogers opted for London rivals Chelsea, Barcola moved to Liverpool and Vinicius Jr has stayed at Real Madrid.
Yet reigning champions Arsenal have started this season as strongly as they finished 2025-26, when they celebrated their first Premier League title for 22 years.

articles.title: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller
articles.summary: Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline.
body: Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches.
But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory.
The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup.

Team GB&I needed a quick start to produce any sort of comeback and they delivered after Stuart Grehan, Luke Poulter - son of former Ryder Cup star Ian - Jack Whaley and Tyler Weaver all won their matches.

articles.title: 'Just unheard of! - Antonelli's miracle win likened to 'walking on water'
articles.summary: On a Monza weekend that had already produced one implausible result in qualifying, Italy's new young star Kimi Antonelli delivered a second in Sunday's thrilling race to ensure its own prominent place in Formula 1's history books.
body: Of course, unlike surprise pole position sitter Pierre Gasly - who had never previously qualified at the head of an F1 grid in 190 appearances spent in mostly midfield cars - the 20-year-old Antonelli has become a fixture at the head of the field this year.

Sunday represented the seventh race win of the Mercedes driver's increasingly-impressive second of Formula 1 and one which extended what stood as a 59-point championship lead to a joint season-high 66 points.

But by winning from the second-lowest grid position in F1's 76-year history - 19th place - and beating a team-mate and chief title rival in George Russell who had started from the front row, Antonelli ensured it was anything but just another win.
And that's before you even consider the local factor too - Antonelli ended a 60-year wait for an Italian to win their home Grand Prix again.

articles.title: Arsenal edge out Chelsea in pulsating London derby
articles.summary: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the first real major Premier League heavyweight clash of the new campaign - in an early contender for game of the season.
body: Both London rivals produced a Sunday afternoon treat which rubberstamped Arsenal's credentials as the team to beat - and Chelsea's as worthy challengers for the top honours.

A pulsating game started right from the off as Morgan Rogers - sought after by Arsenal this summer - crashed new club Chelsea ahead after just 77 seconds. That poked the bear of the champions - who produced a response.
After Riccardo Calafiori saw a goal disallowed for offside, former Blue Kai Havertz got his fourth goal against his old club for Arsenal with a strike from the edge of the box.
But despite a dominant Arsenal display, Chelsea still went inches away from a second as Rogers curled wide and Pedro Neto hit the post.
